# GEO report: trailhead

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

I read the code only. Bash was denied, so I used file reads, and that was enough for a code audit. I sampled `/`, `/guides` and `/admin`. `/admin` is deliberately hidden (`noindex`, disallowed in `robots.txt`, not in the sitemap), so I treated it as intentional and left it out of the route counts.

## Code score: 46–54/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 21 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 10.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 46. High = (10.5 + 2) ÷ 23 × 100 = 54.

The site renders only in the browser, hides `/guides` from search, and gives every page the same title and description. The one unknown is whether the canonical (the "main address" tag) is intended, because no site domain is declared anywhere. No blocker cap applied, because not every sampled route is noindex.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Render pages on the server instead of only in the browser (GEO-003)
- **Why it matters:** many crawlers read only the first HTML the server sends. With client-only rendering, they see an empty page.
- **Where:** `nuxt.config.ts:2`
- **What the code says:** `ssr: false,`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 59–67

### 2. Stop marking `/guides` as noindex (GEO-014)
- **Why it matters:** `/guides` is in your sitemap, but a server header tells search engines not to index it. That is a mixed signal.
- **Where:** `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`
- **What the code says:** `setResponseHeader(event, 'X-Robots-Tag', 'noindex');`
- **Size:** Small (delete the middleware, or limit it to private paths)
- **Score after this:** 52–61

### 3. Make the `Sitemap:` line in robots.txt an absolute URL (GEO-011)
- **Why it matters:** crawlers expect a full address. A relative path may be ignored, so they may not find your sitemap.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:4`
- **What the code says:** `Sitemap: /sitemap.xml`
- **Size:** Small (use `https://trailhead.example/sitemap.xml`, or your real domain)
- **Score after this:** 54–63

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and small | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, valid lines, tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed (assumed goal: be found) | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2`, only `/admin` is disallowed |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts:3`, `/guides` is noindex (1 of 2 routes clear) |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical per page | Can't tell | Not run | No canonical anywhere, and no site origin declared |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | Not run | `nuxt.config.ts:2`, `ssr: false` (0 of 2 routes) |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap valid and discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:4`, relative `Sitemap:` line; `public/sitemap.xml` itself is valid |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Problem | Not run | `app.vue:2` and `nuxt.config.ts:6` give every page the same title and description (0 of 2 routes); `lang` is set at `nuxt.config.ts:5` |
| GEO-016 | Routes reachable via real links | Problem | Not run | `pages/index.vue:8`, `<button @click="router.push('/guides')">` (0 of 1 routes) |
| GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | Not run | `server/middleware/headers.ts` sets only `noindex`, no `nosnippet` |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Not run | Read `app.vue` and `pages/*.vue`: no images, and the button has text |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | Absent, not scored |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (information only) | Not applicable | Not run | None, not scored |

## Can't tell from code

- **GEO-015 (canonical):** no canonical tag exists, and no site domain is declared. The sitemap uses `trailhead.example`, which looks like a placeholder. Tell me your real domain and I can confirm. If I add absolute canonicals on it, the rule moves to Clear: 46–54 becomes 55–55 after the other fixes are counted separately.
- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Hosting:** the `X-Robots-Tag` middleware only takes effect if it runs on your host. Static hosting would skip it. That doesn't change the result, because the code does set the header.

## Assumptions

- You want search and AI search tools to find the site, and there is no `geo.config.json`.
- `/admin` is meant to be private.
- Blocking `/admin` and keeping it out of the sitemap is a deliberate choice, so I didn't count it.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Also worth fixing, at 2 points each: give each page its own title and description (GEO-012), and turn the `/guides` button into a real `<NuxtLink to="/guides">` (GEO-016).

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
